prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” AI video ad maker — the right tool depends on your goals (social short ads vs long-form repurposing), whether you need AI presenters/avatars, your budget, and the level of creative control you want. Below are top choices by common use case, with quick pros/cons to help you pick.

If you want an AI presenter / talking-head ads
- Synthesia
  - Pros: very realistic AI avatars, 120+ languages, easy script → video workflow, good for explainer/brand messages.
  - Cons: costlier for heavy use, limited advanced visual editing.
- HeyGen (formerly DeepBrain / similar tools)
  - Pros: cheaper than Synthesia in many tiers, good for fast presenter videos.
  - Cons: slightly less polished avatars for some use cases.

If you’re turning long videos into short social ads or repurposing content
- Opus Clip / Vidyo.ai / Pictory
  - Pros: automated highlights + captions, optimized aspect ratios for Reels/TikTok/YouTube Shorts, very fast.
  - Cons: less granular creative control; some trimming may be needed.

If you want simple, template-driven social ads with lots of stock assets
- Canva / InVideo / Promo.com
  - Pros: huge template libraries, easy resizing, stock footage and music included, cheap/free tiers.
  - Cons: less AI magic for talking heads; more manual design work.

If you want advanced generative visuals and creative editing
- Runway
  - Pros: powerful generative tools (text-to-video, background removal, inpainting), good for unique visuals.
  - Cons: learning curve; more experimental.

If you need tight audio editing, transcription, or overdub
- Descript
  - Pros: excellent transcript-based editing, overdub voice cloning, great for repurposing podcasts or interviews into ads.
  - Cons: not focused on templates or rapid social ad creation.

If you need dynamic, personalized ad variations at scale
- Shakr / VidMob (or platforms that offer dynamic creative optimization)
  - Pros: built for performance advertising, A/B testing, scalable variations per audience.
  - Cons: more enterprise-focused and pricier.

How to choose
- Use-case: presenter, repurposing, social templates, or experimental visuals?
- Output channels: TikTok/Reels vs YouTube vs TV/Display.
- Budget & scale: free/trial OK? Need many variations?
- Languages & voiceovers: required?
- Level of control: fully manual vs automated.

Quick recommendation
- For presenter-led brand ads: try Synthesia (or HeyGen to save cost).
- For fast social short ads from long content: try Opus Clip or Pictory.
- For easy template-driven social ads: try Canva or InVideo.
- For creative generative visuals: try Runway.

If you tell me what you’re making (ad length, channel, need for avatar, monthly budget, and number of variations), I’ll recommend the single best option and a backup and can suggest a sample workflow.
